title: Double drums, early traps and the first hi-hat
summary: He explains that double drums meant two men, describes cymbal attachments on the foot pedal, and credits Ray Bauduc with the first low hi-hat.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Early drum kits and the gear drummers used

blocks.x: Well, before I forget, you mentioned that, uh, word double drums. I've heard Papa Lane talk about that. Just what do you mean?

Well, instead of having one man play both drums, you know, with the foot pedal and that, well, you had, you had two men. One played the bass drum and one played the snare drum. Not only in parades, now this was for any, any, any dances at all. Because there was no such thing as the foot pedal there.
Yeah. So when they used double drums, they used two men.
They used two men. Yeah. That's, what I meant by.
I didn't know something. Could've meant that one guy played two drums, snare and the bass.
No, no. The same number. No. No. And, uh, when, uh, when, uh, when the, when the, when the foot pedals first came out and, uh, and, uh, and, uh, then you could use the traps. They called them traps.

You didn't call them accessories. They called them traps. And you could, uh, you could use the cymbal on top and, and, and, and the, and the foot pedal. And they always had a little, a little, a little attachment on, on the, on the pedal there. And you'd put a cymbal down on the side of the bass drum and it would hit the, hit the bass drum and the cymbal simultaneously like that. You know, to give that, that little whatchacom. And, uh, there's no, no such thing as, uh, is, uh, hi-hats or anything like that. Cause the first, the first, uh, the things that resembled hi-hats at all were, were, uh, Ray Badu, uh, designed the first one that I've ever seen in my life. There was two cymbals with a, with a pedal, but down, not, not up like they are now, but down, down, down, down like that. And they would hit together like that.
Just about a foot off the floor?

Just about a foot off the floor, yeah. And Ray designed the first one that I've ever seen. And I think it was Ludwig, old man Ludwig, you know, the WFL. I think he was the one who put the first one out. And then later came the, the, the hi-hat. But then they, they, they'd call you, if you played, uh, the, the both drums at one time, they'd call you a trap drum in those days, you see.
